observations.resolution: Revise how_they_met to: 'Met around 2020 when Mateo was at Camp Creek Elementary (Keisha's school); they bonded at a PTA meeting over a shared Zora Neale Hurston paperback, and Maria brought Keisha into the book club that fall.' circle_level_observations.text: All five most intensive daily-text contacts named in the interview are accounted for: Cristina (Q05 daily), Esperanza (Q05 daily logistics), two siblings from the family group chat (Q05, Q25), and a book club / race-ally friend (Q07, Q26, Q30). Occupations span health care, education, semi-retired housekeeping, medical billing, and diesel mechanics. Matches preferences.cultural_and_linguistic 'bridge-builder' framing.

Hector (husband) is not in the circle. This is defensible because he lives in the same household (Q11, Q51) — most marital communication is in-person or voice, not text — and the prompt targets 'personal text messages,' which tends to undercount cohabiting spouses. Worth noting but not a correction.

Mother-in-law Flor (Q05: weekly Sunday video call from Monterrey) was considered but not included; weekly video contact is lower-intensity than the five chosen daily/near-daily texters. Defensible omission.
Youngest brother Tomás (Q05, Q11: couch-crashes monthly) and compadres Rogelio/Maricela (Q05) are plausible alternates if one of the five slots were contested. No change needed.
Ms. Deborah (Q07, mentor / arts center director) was excluded because that relationship is primarily the professional channel the prompt asks to filter out. Correct exclusion.
